title: Jelly Roll Morton, riverboat bands and Alphonso Trent's sidemen
summary: Crawford never met Jelly Roll Morton, recalls the levee bands, and describes Alphonso Trent's sidemen such as banjoist Crooke.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Did you ever meet -- speaking of composers, did you ever meet Jelly Roll Morton?
Jelly Roll Morton, band man from Kansas City?

Oh. No, I didn't, but I knew a lot about him. I didn't have the pleasure of meeting him. But as I said, coming up in those river boat bands, they were natural musicians, sound, color, they were just -- it was amazing to stand on that levee in Memphis, Tennessee and listen to those bands coming through Memphis, and playing, and docking those boats. Oh, yeah. Alphonso Trent.
Yeah, you mention his band a lot. You must have really liked that man.

Certainly I did. He had A.C. Godley (Sensational) Gardley on drums. Alphonso Trent. Crook was his banjo player. He didn't play guitar in that band, he played banjo. Chester Clark, first trumpet player. Oh, yeah, a fellow was

telling me -- Arthur Hines, again, that he used to go -- Crooke finally settled in New York as a super in an apartment building. Say he used to go by and they'd play cards together. Crooke, banjo player formerly with Alphonso Trent. And good banjo player, rhythm-wise. Whatever way he played on the banjo. But it was good.
